Work ONLY inside /opt/nxeon-wt-giveitems (a pre-created git worktree, branch `feature/freemc-giveitems`, off the Nxeon hosting platform's main repo). Do NOT touch /opt/nxeon or any other /opt/nxeon-wt-* directory — those are other people's/other agents' work happening concurrently. `node_modules` and `.env` in your worktree are symlinks to the main repo (normal) — but NEVER run `git add -A` there, it's a known hazard that can corrupt the main repo's real `node_modules` through the symlink. Only ever `git add` the exact file paths you changed.

This is a real production hosting business (Next.js/TypeScript/Prisma/Postgres). Free Minecraft hosting product; customers get a personal Minecraft server on a shared host (`freemc-host`).

## The bug

The customer used the dashboard's "give item to player" / inventory editor tool while their server's active game type was SkyBlock, and the item did NOT get added to the player's inventory. No error was reported to them — it just silently failed to work.

## Relevant history (so you don't re-discover it)

Earlier this session, this same give-items tool had a DIFFERENT bug: RCON's `/list` output was leaking ANSI color escape codes into player names (e.g. `papiguapo\x1b[0m`), which broke player-name validation and caused a "Pick a valid player" error. That was fixed by stripping ANSI codes once at the source, in `sendRcon` inside `lib/free-minecraft-control.ts`:
```ts
const ANSI_ESCAPE_RE = /\x1b\[[0-9;]*m/g;
// ... return { ok: true, response: r.stdout.replace(ANSI_ESCAPE_RE, "").trim() };
```
That fix is already live. This is a NEW, separate report — the tool now presumably finds a valid player, but the actual `/give` doesn't land in their inventory when SkyBlock is the active game type specifically.

## Investigate

1. Find the give-items action and UI — search for something like `lib/actions-freemc-inventory.ts` or similar, and its corresponding component (likely under `components/customer/freemc/` or `components/admin/`). Read exactly what RCON command it issues (probably `/give <player> <item> <amount>` or similar via `sendRcon`).
2. Live-test it directly against the real test container to reproduce and diagnose. There's a real active test server: container `mc-free-cmrztujaw0002hlazl58i3lsi` (owned by test user `cmrztujaw0002hlazl58i3lsi`), currently running SkyBlock, with a real person actively testing on it — so be READ-MOSTLY and careful: it's fine to run `/give papiguapo dirt 1`-style test commands via RCON to reproduce (that's a normal, low-risk gameplay action), but don't touch their world files, don't restart/recreate the container, and don't run destructive commands.

SSH pattern (host is looked up from the DB, not env vars):
```ts
import { db } from "./lib/db"; // relative to /opt/nxeon-wt-giveitems
import { withServerSsh, exec } from "./lib/ssh-exec";
const host = await db.server.findFirst({ where: { hostname: "freemc-host" }, select: { id:true, rootPassword:true, rootPasswordEnc:true, sshPort:true, dedicatedIp:{select:{address:true}} } });
await withServerSsh(host!, async (conn) => {
  const r = await exec(conn, 'docker exec mc-free-cmrztujaw0002hlazl58i3lsi rcon-cli "give papiguapo dirt 1"', 10000);
  console.log(r.stdout, r.stderr);
});
```
Run via `npx tsx -e "..."` from inside `/opt/nxeon-wt-giveitems`.

3. Plausible root causes to check (don't assume — verify each against the real server):
   - Does the actual `/give` RCON command executed by the app match Paper's real command syntax exactly (item id format, namespace prefix like `minecraft:dirt` vs bare `dirt`, amount ordering)? Check `docker exec <container> rcon-cli "give papiguapo minecraft:dirt 1"` directly and see if IT works, to isolate "our command is wrong" vs "something about SkyBlock blocks it."
   - Is the player's inventory actually full (give silently fails/drops on the ground if full — check if the item just landed on the ground near the player rather than in their inventory, which might look like "nothing happened" from the panel's perspective but isn't actually a bug)?
   - Does IridiumSkyblock or any of its plugin stack (EssentialsX, LuckPerms, VaultUnlocked) have any protection/permission system that could block server-console-issued `/give` commands specifically within the `iridiumskyblock` world/dimension (island protection systems sometimes block ALL block/item placement including console-originated ones)? Check the live server logs (`docker exec <container> tail -100 /data/logs/latest.log` or `docker logs <container> --tail 100`) right as you issue a test give command, and look for any plugin warning/denial message.
   - Is the app looking up/targeting the player by a name or UUID that doesn't match who's actually online in the `iridiumskyblock` world specifically (e.g., a stale online-player list, or a world-scoped lookup that misses players outside the default world)?
   - Check `docker exec <container> rcon-cli "list"` to see the exact online player name format at the moment of the bug, compare against what the app's code passes into its `/give` command.

4. Root-cause it with actual evidence (live command output, log lines), not a guess. Then fix it in the code.

## Constraints — important

- Run `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm run build` inside `/opt/nxeon-wt-giveitems` before finishing.
- Commit with a clear message explaining the actual root cause you found (not a guess) and the fix. Do NOT merge to main, do NOT touch staging, do NOT run deploy/promote scripts — a human handles integration separately.
- Report back: the confirmed root cause (with the evidence that proved it), the fix, files touched, and confirm you committed on `feature/freemc-giveitems`.

615	  conn: Client,
616	  containerName: string,
617	  timeoutMs = 110_000,

622	  await sleep(3_000);

658	export async function recreateGameTypeContainer(
659	  conn: Client,
660	  params: {
661	    containerName: string;
662	    dataPath: string;
663	    subdomain: string;
664	    domain: string;
665	    ramMb: number;
666	    ownerId: string;
667	    gameType: FreeMcGameType;
668	    gameTypeKey: string;
669	    gameMode: FreeMcGameMode;
670	    /** Extra env vars layered on top of the type's own (e.g. the Mod Menu's
671	     *  merged MODRINTH_PROJECTS list) — last-write-wins over the type's env. */
672	    extraEnv?: Record<string, string>;
673	  },
674	): Promise<{ ok: boolean; error?: string }> {
675	  const jvmRatio = params.gameType.kind === "plugins" ? 0.7 : 0.85; // plugins need more non-heap headroom — see FREEMC_PLUGIN_MC_VERSION's neighboring history
676	  const cpus = params.gameType.kind === "plugins" ? 2 : 1; // see recreatePresetContainer's note on mc-router's fixed 60s wake timeout
677	  // The global free_minecraft_ram_mb setting (1024 by default) is sized for
678	  // the properties-only presets — plugins-kind ones (EssentialsX + LuckPerms
679	  // + Vault + a type's own plugins, up to 6 loaded dimensions on something
680	  // like SkyBlock) run noticeably heavier and were found live to OOM-kill a
681	  // short while AFTER printing "Done" at that ceiling — not during boot, so
682	  // the old shallow "still alive 15s after docker run" check never caught it,
683	  // and the fix wasn't the plugins themselves (confirmed by re-testing with
684	  // WorldEdit removed — same crash, same timing) or --cpus. It really is a
685	  // sizing problem: 1536m/0.7 ran the same SkyBlock config stable for 100s+
686	  // post-boot with ONE player — but confirmed live it's still not enough
687	  // once a SECOND player joins: memory climbed to 90% (1.355GB/1.5GB) during
688	  // the second player's own island-creation schematic paste (world-gen +
689	  // chunk load + plugin bookkeeping for two islands across up to 6
690	  // dimensions at once), and the container was killed twice in that window
691	  // before settling. 2560m/0.7 gives real headroom for that case; the free
692	  // tier is a shared/social product, so "two friends on one server" is the
693	  // common case, not an edge case. Bump container memory for plugin-kind
694	  // presets specifically rather than raising the global default (which
695	  // properties-only presets don't need).
696	  const ramMb = params.gameType.kind === "plugins" ? Math.max(params.ramMb, 2560) : params.ramMb;
697	  const jvmMb = Math.max(256, Math.round(ramMb * jvmRatio));
698	
699	  const envVars = { ...envForGameType(params.gameType), ...(params.extraEnv ?? {}), LEVEL: params.gameTypeKey };
700	  const envFlags = Object.entries(envVars)
701	    .map(([k, v]) => `-e ${k}=${shellQuote(v)}`)
702	    .join(" ");
703	
704	  await exec(conn, `docker rm -f ${shellQuote(params.containerName)}`, 30_000);
705	  const cmd = [
706	    "docker run -d",
707	    `--name ${shellQuote(params.containerName)}`,
708	    "--network freemc",
709	    `--memory=${ramMb}m --memory-swap=${ramMb}m --cpus=${cpus}`,
710	    `--label mc-router.host=${shellQuote(`${params.subdomain}.${params.domain}`)}`,
711	    `-v ${shellQuote(params.dataPath)}:/data`,
712	    `-e EULA=TRUE -e TYPE=${params.gameType.type ?? "VANILLA"} -e ONLINE_MODE=FALSE`,
713	    params.gameType.kind === "plugins" ? `-e VERSION=${shellQuote(FREEMC_PLUGIN_MC_VERSION)}` : "",
714	    `-e MEMORY=${jvmMb}m`,
715	    `-e ENABLE_RCON=true -e RCON_PASSWORD=${shellQuote(rconPasswordFor(params.ownerId))}`,
716	    envFlags,
717	    "itzg/minecraft-server",
718	  ].join(" ");
719	  const run = await exec(conn, cmd, 90_000); // plugin downloads can take longer than a plain boot
720	  if (run.code !== 0) return { ok: false, error: run.stderr || "docker run failed" };
721	
722	  const ready = await waitForServerReady(conn, params.containerName);
723	  if (!ready.ok) return ready;
724	
725	  // IridiumSkyblock ships with `islandCreateOnJoin: false` — a customer who
726	  // joins fresh just spawns in the plain overworld terrain (which, since
727	  // that's Paper's stock generator, looks exactly like Vanilla), with no
728	  // floating island and no indication one exists to create. Confirmed live:
729	  // a customer reported "joined the server but it has vanilla loaded even
730	  // though I chose skyblock" — this is why. The config file only exists
731	  // after the plugin's first boot (it writes its own defaults), so this has
732	  // to run as a post-boot patch, not something bakeable into the image/env.
733	  // Patched HERE — right after the first readiness wait, BEFORE
734	  // applyModeProperties's own restart below — so that ONE restart picks up
735	  // both this and the mode properties together. An earlier version patched
736	  // this AFTER applyModeProperties with its own separate restart+wait, which
737	  // meant a SkyBlock switch chained three full boot-and-wait cycles back to
738	  // back (each 40-90s) — confirmed live to run past whatever the browser/
739	  // client was willing to wait for, so the switch would actually succeed
740	  // server-side a couple minutes later while the customer had already seen
741	  // a timeout/error and given up. Two cycles instead of three meaningfully
742	  // shortens that window; a config patch with no plugin process running yet
743	  // to pick it up costs nothing extra by itself.
744	  //
745	  // `islandCreateOnJoin` alone was not the whole bug: it only makes the
746	  // plugin create the island in the background. Whether the player actually
747	  // gets TELEPORTED there is a separate key, `spawnOnIsland`, which also
748	  // ships `false` — so even with an island silently created, the player was
749	  // left standing in that same plain default-generator "skyblock" level,
750	  // which is exactly the "shows active on skyblock but loads vanilla world"
751	  // report. Both keys have to be true for a fresh join to actually land the
752	  // player on their island.
753	  //
754	  // `paster: "worldedit"` is a third default-config landmine: this server
755	  // stack never installs WorldEdit (the boot log warns "selected paster
756	  // [worldedit] is not available, available choices are [internalAsync]"),
757	  // and running `/is create` against that misconfiguration killed the whole
758	  // Minecraft process outright — instant death, no Java exception, no JVM
759	  // crash dump, exit code -1 from mc-server-runner. Confirmed live: with
760	  // `paster: "internalAsync"` (the only paster actually available) patched
761	  // in, `/is create` completes normally. internalAsync is the plugin's own
762	  // built-in pasting implementation and needs no other plugin installed.
763	  if (params.gameTypeKey === "skyblock") {
764	    const patch = await exec(
765	      conn,
766	      `docker exec ${shellQuote(params.containerName)} sed -i ` +
767	        `-e 's/islandCreateOnJoin: false/islandCreateOnJoin: true/' ` +
768	        `-e 's/spawnOnIsland: false/spawnOnIsland: true/' ` +
769	        `-e 's/paster: "worldedit"/paster: "internalAsync"/' ` +
770	        `/data/plugins/IridiumSkyblock/configuration.yml`,
771	      10_000,
772	    );
773	    if (patch.code !== 0) {
774	      console.error("[free-minecraft] SkyBlock island-spawn config patch failed (non-fatal):", patch.stderr);
775	    }
776	  }
777	
778	  const modeApplied = await applyModeProperties(conn, params.containerName, params.ownerId, params.gameMode);
779	  if (!modeApplied.ok) return { ok: false, error: modeApplied.error || "Could not apply the active game mode." };
780	
781	  // applyModeProperties ends in a `docker restart`, which re-runs the exact
782	  // same boot sequence as the `docker run` above — needs the same real
783	  // readiness wait, not a fixed few-second sleep. This restart is also what
784	  // picks up the SkyBlock config patch above, if it ran.
785	  const readyAfterMode = await waitForServerReady(conn, params.containerName);
786	  if (!readyAfterMode.ok) {
787	    return { ok: false, error: readyAfterMode.error || "Server didn't come back up after applying the active game mode." };
788	  }
789	
790	  return { ok: true };
791	}

## Summary

**Confirmed root cause:** The give-item RCON command (`item replace entity <player> <slot> with <item> <count>`) was silently being intercepted by **EssentialsX's own `/item` command** instead of reaching vanilla's `/item replace entity ... with ...` handler. EssentialsX is bundled on the SkyBlock and Towny presets (`lib/free-minecraft-control.ts` env: `iridiumskyblock,vaultunlocked,essentialsx,luckperms,viaversion` for skyblock). Bukkit gives a plugin's command registration priority over the vanilla command with the same unqualified label, so the bare `item` command was always routed to Essentials.

**Evidence gathered:**
1. Pulled EssentialsX's real `plugin.yml` from a jar already on the fleet (`/opt/freemc/servers/timingtest/plugins/EssentialsX-2.22.0.jar`) — it registers its own `item` command: "Spawn an item", usage `/<command> <item|numeric> [amount]`, which gives an item to the *sender* (not a named target) — a completely different command than vanilla's.
2. Found the customer's actual failing SkyBlock session in rotated logs (`/opt/freemc/servers/cmt8pa1d70002hln2pxq6ud0i/logs/2026-08-25-8.log.gz`), showing the exact command tagged `[Essentials] Rcon issued server command: /item replace entity papiguapo hotbar.0 with minecraft:wooden_pickaxe 1` — the `[Essentials]` tag proves Essentials' handler processed it (it tried to parse "replace" as an item id, and since RCON/console isn't a player, had nowhere to put anything anyway) — never reaching vanilla's slot-replace logic. `rcon-cli` exits 0 regardless, so `sendRcon` reported `ok: true`, explaining why no error surfaced to the customer.
3. This also retroactively explains the earlier (already-fixed) ANSI-codes-in-player-names bug: it was Essentials' own colorized `list` command answering RCON, not vanilla's — same shadowing mechanism, different command.
4. Live-verified the fix: `minecraft:item replace entity ...` resolves to the real vanilla handler — same "Invalid name or UUID" vanilla error text as the unprefixed form when run against the currently-running Prison test container (which has no EssentialsX loaded).

**Fix:** In `/opt/nxeon-wt-giveitems/lib/actions-freemc-inventory.ts`, prefixed the RCON command with `minecraft:` (`minecraft:item replace entity ...`), which forces Bukkit to dispatch to the vanilla command regardless of what any plugin has registered under the bare `item` label — fixes it for SkyBlock and Towny (the only two presets that bundle EssentialsX) without touching any other preset's behavior.
